purpose: Authoritative schema-rules contract for VIGIL as a public evidence-to-repair observatory for observations, research artefacts, failure modes, proposals, and implemented patch notes. Source evidence remains embedded in the relevant record; ecosystem persistence, CAM repair, and implementation verification are represented separately. Interpretive provenance identifies the AI analytical reviewer, human governance editor, capability profile, source modality, primary-artefact access, and review limitations.

individual_records: source_records is the only canonical source-evidence block in individual records.
source_data is forbidden in individual records.
source_data.sources is forbidden in individual records.
linked_records.external_references must not duplicate the primary evidence source already held in source_records.
Source evidence belongs in source_records within the substantive record it evidences; it is not a separate VIGIL record class.
An OBS record must preserve a material unresolved governance proposition and must not merely duplicate evidence for an existing FM, PROP, or PATCH.
Internal curator instructions such as 'add this incident to' or 'do not amend in this pass' are forbidden in public record content.
Each source record must state evidence_modality.
Each source record must state primary_artefact_access, including whether direct primary review occurred.
A transcript, screenshot, summary, or human description must not be represented as equivalent to direct audiovisual or interaction review.
Each source record must state source_residence so external incident evidence is distinguishable from CAM/VIGIL provenance.
Each source record must state source_role so evidence, governance basis, taxonomy basis, implementation evidence, verification evidence, and record cross-references are not rendered interchangeably.
External-evidence interfaces must require source_residence external; absence of a VIGIL identifier is not sufficient evidence of external residence.
CAM-internal and VIGIL-internal sources remain valid provenance but must not be rendered as external incident evidence.
generated_registers: Generated registers may contain derived source_summary fields.
source_summary is derived from source_records and is not maintained by individual record files.
canonical_source_url_status_values: available / canonical main-branch confirmation pending exact line review
VIGIL local / pending public record URL if applicable
available / pending archive and evidence verification

research.description: Non-binding research artefact that may originate an evidence-to-repair chain in place of, or alongside, an observation.
research.storage_format: Markdown with required JSON front matter
research.authority_boundary: Research records preserve analysis and evidence. They do not create CAM authority; authority arises through a linked proposal and implemented PATCH.

published_quality_contract.corroboration_rule: A published record labelled corroborated or externally corroborated must draw from at least two publisher domains or expressly qualify the within-publisher corroboration basis in corroboration_scope.
published_quality_contract.routing_rule: Short, single-source or lightly synthesized material belongs in a source record or observation unless expanded into a substantive research artefact.

observation.description: Material unresolved governance observation / early warning record; not a duplicate source-evidence container.
observation.cam_routing: Use related_or_similar_* fields only. OBS preserves a substantive unresolved governance proposition and uncertainty; source evidence for an existing record belongs in that record's source_records.

failure_mode.cam_routing: Use affected_* fields for triage-relevant CAM routing.
failure_mode.repair_status_interpretation: repair_status describes the CAM-side governance response only. It must not be read as proof that an external ecosystem failure has ceased.
failure_mode.repair_basis_interpretation: repair_status.repair_basis identifies what establishes an actual CAM-side repair. Corpus coverage states such as no-confirmed-coverage and partial-coverage belong only in corpus_coverage.classification.
failure_mode.corpus_coverage_interpretation: no-confirmed-coverage means a corpus assessment was performed and no sufficient direct current-corpus control was confirmed. verification-pending means the assessment remains incomplete. A missing corpus_coverage block is invalid rather than equivalent to either state.

proposal.cam_routing: Use target_* fields. A PROP must not claim implementation as a completed patch.

patch.description: Traceable Caelestis implementation record: either a corpus amendment or an explicit retrospective reliance on pre-existing control. VIGIL maintenance is outside the PATCH class.
patch.cam_routing: Use changed_* fields. PATCH records require commit-addressed literal Caelestis text. VIGIL schema, template, validator, workflow, registry, documentation, and interface maintenance is never a corpus PATCH.
patch.literal_text_rule: Every corpus entry must reproduce wording exactly from source.commit:source.path. A verified entry sets exact_text_match true; cross-repository validation must fail on a paraphrase or unresolved Git object.
patch.retrospective_rule: Pre-existing coverage uses implementation_type pre-existing-control and change_kind relied-upon, quotes the relevant wording, and does not imply that the doctrine originated on the PATCH date.
patch.branch_rule: A branch-only implementation remains active and must not be represented as closed-actioned or canonical-main.
patch.array_reconciliation_rule: Amendment and relied-upon instrument sets in corpus_implementation.entries must exactly match repair_provenance and cam_internal routing.

enum: civil society safety assessment / public-interest report

system_context_rules.description: system_context describes the observed/proposed system, platform, product, service, runtime, interface, deployment, or governance corpus using normalised field names.
system_context_rules.specific_model_or_runtime_rule: Non-empty string; intentionally not an enum because runtime names and tool-augmented modes drift frequently.
system_context_rules.interface_surface_rule: Non-empty string or array of non-empty strings describing where or how behaviour appears.

cam_internal_rules.description: cam_internal describes CAM routing, targets, affected areas, or changed components.

cam_failure_taxonomy.taxonomy_reference: CAM-EQ2026-OPERATIONS-003-SUP-01 Appendix B: Runtime & Governance Failure Taxonomy
cam_failure_taxonomy.derived_from: CAM-EQ2026-OPERATIONS-003-SUP-01 Appendix B: Runtime & Governance Failure Taxonomy, including §3.11 Economic & Legitimacy Failures as economic-legitimacy.

generated_register_rules.pruning: Generated index manifests prune empty arrays, empty strings, empty objects, and nulls while preserving meaningful uncertainty values.
generated_register_rules.index_entry_contract: Generated type indexes and the master registry contain lean collapsed-list metadata plus canonical record location fields only. Detailed summaries and full evidence/context structures remain in individual canonical record JSON files.
type_specific_list_fields: failure severity, likelihood, classification, and triage filter fields
patch/change type/status and verification filter fields
research status, method, governance purpose, domains, and linked-record fields

linked_records_rules.standards: linked_records.standards is reserved for external standards, laws, regulatory instruments, technical standards, and external governance references. CAM instrument IDs such as CAM-BS* and CAM-EQ* belong in cam_internal routing fields, using related/similar for observations, affected for failure modes, target for proposals, and changed for patches.
linked_records_rules.research: linked_records.research contains VIGIL research artefact IDs. An evidence-to-repair chain may originate in an Observation, Research record, or both. Research is evidentiary and non-binding; authority arises only through the linked proposal and implemented PATCH.
linked_records_rules.reciprocity: Research front-matter links to observations, failure modes, proposals, or patch notes must be reciprocated by the target record in linked_records.research.
linked_records_rules.repair_scope: A proposal or PATCH has zero or one primary failure mode by default. A governance-origin or research-origin proposal may have none. Multiple resolved failure modes are an explicit exception requiring a rationale; a PATCH must also provide one verification result per resolved failure.
linked_records_rules.contextual_relations: linked_records.contextual_relations contains typed, visible, non-transitive context. chain_inclusion must be false. Contextual records must not also appear in authoritative linked-record arrays and must never be interpreted as repaired by the proposal or PATCH.
linked_records_rules.authoritative_chain: Only declared evidence origins, repair_scope failure modes, proposal resolution links, and verified repairing PATCH links participate in evidence-to-repair traversal. Generic related, adjacent, contrast, supporting-mechanism, shared-corpus-area, precedent, and separate-workstream links do not expand the chain.

record_state_rules.purpose: Top-level record_state is the maintainer workflow and pipeline state. It must not be used as a proxy for external ecosystem conditions, CAM repair status, proposal resolution, or corpus coverage.

semantics.draft: Record is being authored and is not yet ready for triage.
semantics.scaffolding: Temporary incomplete record retained only for construction or migration.
semantics.active: A governance decision, evidence action, proposal, or CAM repair still requires attention.
semantics.monitoring: The immediate VIGIL/CAM action is complete or bounded, but recurrence, implementation, or external conformity remains under observation.
semantics.closed-actioned: The record has been routed, implemented, or otherwise actioned and no longer belongs in the active work queue.
semantics.closed-no-action: The evidence is retained but no further action is justified.
semantics.deferred: Action is intentionally postponed and should not appear as current active work.
semantics.superseded: A successor record now carries the active governance work.

class_rules.failure_mode: Unrepaired or partially-repaired failures are active; repaired failures are monitoring; not-actionable failures are closed-no-action; superseded failures are superseded.
class_rules.proposal: Open or routed proposals are active; resolved-by-patch proposals are closed-actioned; closed-no-action, deferred, and superseded resolution states map directly.
class_rules.patch: Canonical-main and historical-canonical patch records may be closed-actioned. Branch-only and unverified patch records remain active. Ecosystem monitoring remains on linked failure or observation records.
class_rules.observation: Observations requiring evidence or routing work are active; routed or actioned observations close; unresolved recurrence or positive-control follow-up is monitoring.

runtime_conformance_rules.description: Optional runtime-bounded evidence objects distinguish an implemented CAM repair from observed conformance or non-conformance in named vendor, platform, runtime, model, client, or interface formations. Runtime names remain open-ended and cross-runtime transfer is never presumed.

runtime_conformance.count_rule: Counts must be non-negative integers and must equal the corresponding detail-array length whenever that array is present.
runtime_conformance.runtime_identifier_rule: vendor, platform, runtime, model, and client values are open-ended non-empty strings; no vendor or runtime names are hard-coded by the validator.

runtime_non_conformance.count_rule: Counts must be non-negative integers and must equal the corresponding detail-array length whenever that array is present.
runtime_non_conformance.runtime_identifier_rule: vendor, platform, runtime, model, and client values are open-ended non-empty strings; no vendor or runtime names are hard-coded by the validator.

runtime_conformance_rules.interpretive_rule: patched means the CAM repair exists; confirmed means intended behaviour was observed in a named runtime; non-confirming means the linked failure remains present or recurred in a named runtime. A non-confirming runtime does not invalidate a patch confirmed elsewhere.

lifecycle_rules.ecosystem_status: Describes whether the external failure remains active, recurring, improving, externally resolved, or unknown.
lifecycle_rules.cam_repair_status: repair_status.status describes CAM's internal response and may be repaired while ecosystem_status remains active or recurring.
lifecycle_rules.verification_status: repair_status.verification_status describes whether the repair is unverified, corpus-verified, observed in one or multiple runtimes, regressed, externally unknown, or not applicable.
lifecycle_rules.non_collapse_rule: No one field may be used to imply both CAM repair completion and external ecosystem resolution.
lifecycle_rules.no_patch_no_repair_rule: A failure with no linked repairing PATCH remains unrepaired and uses repair_basis not-yet-established, even where corpus_coverage identifies adjacent or partial doctrine.
lifecycle_rules.coverage_separation_rule: corpus_coverage.classification may be no-confirmed-coverage, partial-coverage, verification-pending, retrospective-coverage, implemented-repair, or not-applicable without being reused as repair provenance.

corpus_coverage_rules: Every failure mode must state its assessment against a named corpus repository, ref, commit, and assessment date.
Implemented repair and retrospective coverage are CAM-side states and do not imply external adoption or ecosystem resolution.
Retrospective coverage must identify the pre-existing instrument and relevant sections without claiming the doctrine originated on the VIGIL patch date.
Partial-coverage and no-confirmed-coverage classifications must preserve concrete remaining gaps.
no-confirmed-coverage means an assessment was performed and no sufficient direct current-corpus control was confirmed; verification-pending means the assessment remains incomplete.
A coverage assessment must never be inferred solely from thematic similarity; the cited instrument must materially govern the failure mechanism.
patch_trace_rules: PATCH is a signal trace of a governance decision and its Caelestis outcome, not a container for VIGIL maintenance.
Decision chronology belongs in decision_trace; literal implemented or relied-upon corpus wording belongs in corpus_implementation; reconstruction disclosure belongs in record_reconstruction.
record_reconstruction.reconstructed is true only for rebuilt legacy PATCH records and false for records created natively under the trace-first contract.
Narrative, evidence, and interpretive provenance remain preserved below the implementation trace and must not substitute for it.

Each corpus entry names exactly one instrument and canonical path, one section and heading, its change kind, prior wording status, literal resulting wording, commit-addressed source, and verification state.
Retrospective reliance is labelled pre-existing control relied upon—no corpus amendment.
Actioned corpus PATCH records without traceable implementation text are invalid.

Every PATCH must preserve corpus_release_provenance distinguishing the exact implementation corpus state, later canonical state, and published archive release. A current archive citation must not be represented as the historical implementation version without verified release inclusion.

interpretive_provenance_rules.review_history_rule: Append reviews; do not overwrite or retroactively invent earlier reviewer model identities.
interpretive_provenance_rules.chronology_rule: Every review_date must be a valid ISO YYYY-MM-DD date on or after the calendar-date component of record_identity.created (or date_recorded where created is unavailable). A review must never be backdated or attached to a record that did not yet exist.
interpretive_provenance_rules.human_editor_rule: Human governance editorship and CAM adoption authority must be distinguished from routine AI analytical review.

triage_model_rules.doctrine: Current triage priority is mutable operational state. Historical urgency is provenance. Failure severity is classification. Triage status is workflow. Ecosystem monitoring is continuing external observation.

applicability.boundary: OBS records must not contain failure-mode triage. PROP, PATCH, RESEARCH, and LEARN preserve their own class-specific lifecycle fields and must not receive synthetic FM triage blocks.
applicability.migration_phase: Pass 1 documents the target contract and inventory only. Pass 2 adds hard schema and validator enforcement. Pass 3 reconciles records after human review of the inventory.

semantic_dimensions.failure_classification.severity: Inherent or evidenced seriousness of the failure. CAM repair does not reduce severity.
semantic_dimensions.triage.triage_priority: Urgency of outstanding CAM or VIGIL work now; mutable and operational.
semantic_dimensions.triage.triage_status: Current VIGIL workflow state; not a severity or priority synonym.
semantic_dimensions.record_state: Record lifecycle state under the existing lifecycle contract.
semantic_dimensions.ecosystem_status.monitoring_required: Whether the continuing external condition requires observation; independent of current CAM/VIGIL workload.
semantic_dimensions.triage_history: Append-only provenance for evidenced priority/status transitions; historical urgency does not control current sorting.

priority_meanings.P1: High-priority active work that should be addressed next.
priority_meanings.P2: Normal active queue with a defined next action.
priority_meanings.P4: Deferred backlog or possible future task.
priority_meanings.none: No active CAM or VIGIL triage work remains.

transition_history_contract.type: optional append-only array during migration; required for transitions recorded after adoption of this contract
transition_history_contract.actor_rule: changed_by must identify the evidenced actor or authority. Do not attribute AI-led analysis generically to 'VIGIL maintainers' where the reviewing system is known.
transition_history_contract.legacy_rule: Do not fabricate retrospective transitions. A legacy record with only a known current state may omit triage_history until an evidenced transition occurs.

cross_field_invariants: P0, P1, P2, and P3 require a non-empty recommended_next_step.
P0 requires escalation_required to indicate escalation or contain a documented explanation.
monitoring with an active priority requires a concrete monitoring action in recommended_next_step.
triage_priority none is incompatible with active-investigation, repair-in-progress, and verification-required.
A closed record_state requires triage_priority none.
P4 may omit an immediate action only when triage_status is deferred; otherwise a bounded future action or retention reason is required.
separation_rules: Do not derive current priority from severity.
Do not derive severity from priority.
Do not derive current priority from historical triage entries.
Monitoring alone does not justify P0-P4.
A linked proposal or patch does not by itself close the failure-mode workflow.
Registry projection must expose severity, triage_priority, triage_status, monitoring_required, record_state, and repair_status independently.

legacy_values_observed: high; potentially critical where evidence concerns catastrophic harm, systemic risk, fundamental rights or security compromise
severity_migration_review.mapping_boundary: No severity value is rewritten in Pass 1. medium-high, low-to-medium, and conditional prose ratings require record-level judgment. medium to moderate and to be assessed to to-be-assessed remain proposed normalisations for Pass 3 review.
